assumptions: Each selected row is an independent cohort (distinct cohort_id and study).
CI-derived SEs assume a symmetric normal interval at the reported confidence level.
The 90% CI row (r4) is excluded rather than reinterpreted at 95%.
The median/IQR row (r6) is excluded as a different statistic.

Pooling is exploratory on the current data: the original method is followed (DL random effects, 95% normal CI, hours-to-days conversion, one estimate per cohort), but the current table differs from the original review's included set, so this is not a reproduction.

mixed_uncertainty.justification: Rows report either a 95% CI or a direct SE; both are converted to a standard error on the days scale before inverse-variance pooling. The 90% CI row (r4) is excluded rather than harmonized.

research_question: What is the pooled mean incubation period, in days, of the included adult study cohorts?

sensitivity.description: Repeat the pool with a fixed-effect (common-effect) inverse-variance model to assess sensitivity to the random-effects assumption.
sensitivity.name: fixed_effects

sensitivity.description: Repeat the pool with a REML between-study variance estimator to assess sensitivity to the DL estimator.
sensitivity.name: reml

sensitivity.description: Repeat the DL random-effects pool excluding the hours-converted row r5 to assess sensitivity to the unit conversion.
sensitivity.name: exclude_r5

dependence.justification: Each selected row has a distinct cohort_id (cohort-alvarez, cohort-boot, cohort-chen, cohort-ewing) and a distinct study, matching the original method's one-estimate-per-independent-cohort rule.

selection.rationale: Adult cohorts with estimate_measure=mean and a usable uncertainty (reported SE or CI with explicit level). r4 excluded: 90% CI level is not harmonizable to the 95% estimand without an unsupported assumption. r6 excluded: median/IQR is a different statistic per the original method and review exclusions.

source_mapping.quote:
Study-level mean incubation-period estimates were pooled by the inverse-variance
method with a random-effects model, using the DerSimonian-Laird estimator for
between-study variance, and reported with a 95% confidence interval.
One estimate per independent study cohort was retained.

Estimates reported in hours were converted to days by dividing the point
estimate and its standard error by 24.

Estimates reported as a median or as an interquartile range were not pooled
with mean estimates, because they describe a different statistic of the
incubation-period distribution.
